subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Blind Spot Detection
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Blind Spot Detection.

hook.text: Changing lanes seems simple until a car is hiding where your mirrors can't reach.

buildup.text: Blind spots sit just behind your shoulder—visible only if you turn your head to check.

discovery.text: Radar sensors on the rear corners detect vehicles in the blind zone and flash a warning light.

twist.text: Drivers with blind spot alerts are 14 percent less likely to have lane-change crashes.

climax.text: Some systems resist the steering if you signal while a car is hidden alongside you.

punchline.text: A small light on the mirror prevents a massive collision.

quiz.question: Where are blind spot detection sensors usually mounted?
options: On the rear corners of the car
